Spite
SPYTE
n. (malice; ill will with a desire to vex)
Middle English spite, shortened from despite. At Psalm 10:14 it renders Hebrew ka’as (H3708), vexation or provocation.

Definition · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Psalm 10 is the cry of the poor man while the wicked prosper. The wicked man says in his heart that God has forgotten, that He hides His face and will never see it. The psalmist answers him directly: “Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite it with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless” (Psa 10:14). Spite is the small, deliberate cruelty that wants to vex its victim, the provocation that counts on going unnoticed. The verse says three things about it. God sees it, every instance. God will requite it with His own hand, so the injured man need not. And the poor man therefore commits himself to God instead of to revenge. Paul builds on the same ground: “Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord” (Rom 12:19). Christ is the pattern, “who, when he was reviled, reviled not again… but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously” (1Pe 2:23). The answer to spite is not more spite, and not silence about wrong, but a hand placed in God's.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828): SPITE, hatred; rancor; malice; often a sudden fit of ill will, with a desire to vex.

expand to see more

SPITE, noun Hatred; rancor; malice; malignity; malevolence.

SPITE, however, is not always synonymous with these words. It often denotes a less deliberate and fixed hatred than malice and malignity, and is often a sudden fit of ill will excited by temporary vexation.

It is the effect of extreme irritation, and is accompanied with a desire of revenge, or at least a desire to vex the object of ill will.

In spite of, in opposition to all efforts; in defiance or contempt of.

SPITE, verb transitive 1. To be angry or vexed at. 2. To mischief; to vex; to treat maliciously; to thwart.

Key Scripture

Psa 10:14 — "Thou hast seen it; for thou beholdest mischief and spite, to requite it with thy hand: the poor committeth himself unto thee; thou art the helper of the fatherless."

Rom 12:19 — "Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord."

1Pe 2:23 — "Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously:"

Modern Corruption

Spite is rebranded as justified pushback, and the culture of grievance trains people to answer every slight in kind instead of committing the wrong to God.

expand to see more

Online life has made spite a public sport. The wounding remark, the pile-on and the act of revenge are celebrated as standing up for oneself, and the person who declines to retaliate is called weak. Webster's definition fits the age exactly: ill will excited by temporary vexation and accompanied with a desire to vex. What the age calls strength, Scripture calls the flesh.

Psalm 10 does not ask the afflicted to pretend nothing happened. It names the mischief and spite, and it insists that God has seen it and will requite it. That is what frees the believer from vengeance: the account is not dropped but transferred to the Judge. Romans 12 and 1 Peter 2 make the same transfer, and both rest it on the character of God, not on the merit of the offender.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

From despite; Hebrew ka’as (H3708), vexation, provocation, at Psalm 10:14.

expand to see more

Hebrew ka'as (H3708), vexation, grief, provocation, tagged at Psa 10:14.

English spite is a shortened form of despite.

Webster distinguishes spite from settled malice: a sudden fit of ill will.

Psalm 10:14 is the only occurrence of spite in the Authorized Version.

The adverb spitefully appears in the Gospels for the abuse of Christ.

Usage

"thou beholdest mischief and spite"

"names the petty cruelty that wants to vex and expects to go unseen"

"answered by God's sight and God's hand, not by revenge"
